title: Monoidality of the derived inverse image
statement:
Let $u:U\to V$ be a morphism of schemes and $\Lambda$ a commutative
ring. For $K,L\in D(V_{\Et},\Lambda)$ the canonical comparison
morphism

$$
u^{-1}K\kunotimes{\Lambda}u^{-1}L\longrightarrow
u^{-1}\bigl(K\kunotimes{\Lambda}L\bigr)
$$

of [def-kun-derived-tensor] associated with the
inverse image $u^{-1}$ is an
isomorphism, bifunctorial in $K$ and $L$.
(*Source:* Stacks Project, Lemma 21.18.4,
[Tag `07A4`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07A4),
for the morphism of ringed topoi induced by $u$.)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-exact] to $u:U\to V$. This gives the geometric inverse-image/direct-image adjunction on the small etale sites, with finite-limit-preserving inverse image, as required by the ringed-topos theorem. Choose small representatives of these essentially small sites in a universe larger than the scheme universe, and a still larger universe for module sheaves. Put $R=\Lambda_V$ and $S=\Lambda_U$. The underlying constant sheaf of a set $A$ is the coproduct of $A$ copies of the terminal sheaf: sheafification of the corresponding coproduct of terminal presheaves gives exactly the constant-sheaf definition. A left adjoint preserves this coproduct, and finite-limit preservation preserves the terminal object. Thus $u^{-1}\Lambda_V\cong\Lambda_U$. This identification respects addition, multiplication, zero and one: on each constant label it is the identity on $\Lambda$, and on pairs of labels the finite-product comparison gives the same operations. Equip the induced geometric morphism with this ring isomorphism. Its module pullback $u^*M=S\otimes_{u^{-1}R}u^{-1}M$ identifies naturally with $u^{-1}M$, by $a\otimes m\mapsto am$, inverse $m\mapsto1\otimes m$. This is the coefficient inverse image of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image].

By [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact], $u^{-1}$ preserves kernels and cokernels of abelian sheaves. Kernels and cokernels of module sheaves have these underlying abelian kernels and cokernels, with the induced scalar actions, by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Hence the identified module functor $u^*=u^{-1}$ is exact. Applying it termwise gives $H^n(u^{-1}A^\bullet)\cong u^{-1}H^n(A^\bullet)$, since cohomology is a kernel modulo an image and images are kernels of cokernels. It therefore preserves every quasi-isomorphism, without a bound on $A^\bullet$. Take a K-flat resolution $p:P\to A$ with flat terms using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The natural comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] identifies $Lu^*(Q_RA)$ with $Q_S(u^*P)$. The map $u^*p$ is a quasi-isomorphism by exactness, so its localization gives $Lu^*(Q_RA)\cong Q_S(u^{-1}A)$. To check naturality on all complexes rather than only chosen resolutions, use the canonical natural transformation $\epsilon:Lu^*Q_R\to Q_Su^*$ supplied by the same node. Its naturality for $p$ gives $\epsilon_A=Q_S(u^*p)\circ\epsilon_P\circ Lu^*(Q_Rp)^{-1}$. All three factors are isomorphisms, so every $\epsilon_A$ is an isomorphism. Both functors invert quasi-isomorphisms, so this natural isomorphism descends through the derived-category localization; hence $Lu^*$ identifies naturally with the termwise derived inverse image $u^{-1}$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] with $(R,S)=(\Lambda_V,\Lambda_U)$ and the ring isomorphism from step 1. Its hypotheses are the geometric morphism and small ringed sites established there; it applies to the unbounded categories and to arbitrary $K,L$. Replace $Lu^*$ by the identification in step 2. The tensor products here are the K-flat total tensor products of [def-kun-derived-tensor], so this yields a canonical bifunctorial isomorphism $u^{-1}(K\otimes_\Lambda^{\mathbf L}L)\xrightarrow{\sim}u^{-1}K\otimes_\Lambda^{\mathbf L}u^{-1}L$. Its inverse has the direction displayed in the item.

source.place: Tag 07A4, label lemma-pullback-tensor-product, specialized to constant coefficient ring sheaves

proof.text: To identify this inverse with the stated canonical comparison, take K-flat flat-term representatives $P,Q$ of $K,L$. The ringed-topos tensor theorem ensures their pullbacks are K-flat with flat terms and that these total tensors compute both sides. The canonical module comparison sends the tensor of inverse-image local generators $m,n$ to the inverse-image generator $m\otimes n$. Explicitly, under the tensor-formula pullback it is $(a\otimes m)\otimes(b\otimes n)\mapsto ab\otimes(m\otimes n)$; the balanced relations over $R$ and $S$ make this bilinear rule well-defined, and sheafification gives the corresponding sheaf morphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor], in bidegree $(p,q)$ this canonical comparison is the inverse of $u^*(P^p\otimes_RQ^q)\xrightarrow{\sim}u^*P^p\otimes_Su^*Q^q$. The module adjunction makes $u^*$ a left adjoint, so it preserves the direct sums in totalization. Naturality of the degreewise maps makes them commute with both $d_P\otimes1$ and $1\otimes d_Q$; additivity preserves the factor $(-1)^p$. Consequently their direct sum is an isomorphism of total complexes in exactly the displayed direction. This is the comparison used in the proof of Tag 07A4, not an arbitrary isomorphism between its objects. The uniqueness of extension from K-flat flat-term models in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] identifies it on all derived objects. It is simultaneously natural in both arguments; equivalently naturality of the isomorphism in step 3 gives naturality of its inverse by composing the naturality square with inverse components.

lean.note: Specialize A to ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ for Λ : Type (u + 1), [CommRing Λ], and g to u : U ⟶ V of Scheme.{u}. Import WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.Etale.UpperLowerStar.FlatModuleCat for upperStarPreservesFlat_moduleCat; no mathematical flatness assumption is added. The inverse natural isomorphism has the displayed direction u⁻¹K ⊗ᴸ u⁻¹L → u⁻¹(K ⊗ᴸ L). The identification leftDerivedUpperStarIsoMapDerivedCategory identifies L(upperStar A g) with the exact termwise inverse image. The comparison is canonical: leftDerivedUpperStarTensorComparison is defined by deriving the ordinary oplax tensor comparison, and leftDerivedUpperStarTensorNatIso_hom identifies this morphism with the hom of the recorded natural isomorphism. Its inverse is the derived ordinary lax tensor comparison, not an arbitrary chosen isomorphism. Naturality is in both variables because this is an isomorphism in the iterated functor category. The derived tensor is exactly the declaration recorded by def-kun-derived-tensor; the sheaf inverse image is exactly def-weil-pbc-inverse-image.
